source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Problem 3: Pulling force inclined above the horizontal on a rough surface

hints: Resolve vertically: $R + P\sin 30^\circ = 20 \times 10 = 200\text{ N}$.
Express limiting friction in terms of $P$: $F_r = 0.4(200 - 0.5P) = 80 - 0.2P$.
Set up horizontal equation of motion: $P\cos 30^\circ - (80 - 0.2P) = 20 \times 0.8 = 16\text{ N}$.
Rearrange to solve for $P$: $P(\cos 30^\circ + 0.2) = 96$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$R + P\sin 30^\circ = mg$$
$$R + 0.5P = 20(10) = 200$$
$$R = 200 - 0.5P\text{ N}$$

Express friction and apply Newton's second law horizontally:
$$F_r = \mu R = 0.4(200 - 0.5P) = 80 - 0.2P$$
$$P\cos 30^\circ - F_r = ma$$
$$P\cos 30^\circ - (80 - 0.2P) = 20(0.8) = 16$$
$$P(\cos 30^\circ + 0.2) = 16 + 80 = 96$$
$$P\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + 0.2\right) = 96 \implies P(1.0660) = 96 \implies P = 90.0\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Vertical balance:
$$R = mg - P\sin 30^\circ = 200 - 0.5P\text{ N}$$
The upward vertical component reduces surface contact pressure.

Horizontal equation of motion:
$$P\cos 30^\circ - 0.4(200 - 0.5P) = 16$$
$$P(\cos 30^\circ + 0.2) = 96 \implies P \approx 90.0\text{ N}$$
A pulling force of $90.0\text{ N}$ maintains the required acceleration.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves vertically: $R + P\sin 30^\circ = mg \implies R = 20(10) - 0.5P = 200 - 0.5P$.
Applies Newton's second law horizontally: $P\cos 30^\circ - \mu R = ma \implies P\cos 30^\circ - 0.4(200 - 0.5P) = 20(0.8)$.
Solves for $P$: $P(\cos 30^\circ + 0.2) = 16 + 80 = 96 \implies P(1.066) = 96 \implies P = 90.0\text{ N}$.

Set up the horizontal equation of motion: $P\cos 20^\circ - F_r = 8 \times 1.5 = 12\text{ N}$.
Rearrange to solve for $P$: $P(\cos 20^\circ + 0.2\sin 20^\circ) = 28$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$R + P\sin 20^\circ = mg$$
$$R = 8(10) - P\sin 20^\circ = 80 - P\sin 20^\circ$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally:
$$P\cos 20^\circ - F_r = ma$$
$$P\cos 20^\circ - 0.2(80 - P\sin 20^\circ) = 8(1.5)$$
$$P\cos 20^\circ - 16 + 0.2P\sin 20^\circ = 12$$
$$P(\cos 20^\circ + 0.2\sin 20^\circ) = 12 + 16 = 28$$
$$P(0.93969 + 0.06840) = 28 \implies P(1.00809) = 28 \implies P = \frac{28}{1.00809} \approx 26.5\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Vertical balance:
$$R = 80 - P\sin 20^\circ$$
Contact force decreases linearly with $P$.

Solve horizontal equation:
$$P(\cos 20^\circ + 0.2\sin 20^\circ) = 28$$
$$P = \frac{28}{1.0081} \approx 26.5\text{ N}$$
A pull of $26.5\text{ N}$ produces the observed $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ acceleration.

hints: When $P$ is removed, the normal reaction is simply $R = mg = 80\text{ N}$.
The deceleration is $a_2 = \mu g = 0.2 \times 10 = 2.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Initial speed for this braking phase is $u = 9.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, final speed $v = 0$.
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as_2$ to find $s_2 = \frac{81}{4} = 20.25\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the deceleration under friction alone:
$$R_2 = mg = 8 \times 10 = 80\text{ N}$$
$$F_{r,2} = \mu R_2 = 0.2 \times 80 = 16\text{ N}$$
$$a_2 = \frac{F_{r,2}}{m} = \frac{16}{8} = 2.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate the braking distance to rest:
$$v_f^2 = v^2 - 2a_2 s_2$$
$$0 = 9.0^2 - 2(2.0)s_2$$
$$0 = 81 - 4.0 s_2 \implies s_2 = \frac{81}{4.0} = 20.25\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Stage 2 deceleration:
$$a = \mu g = 0.2(10) = 2.0\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Kinematic braking calculation:
$$s_2 = \frac{9.0^2}{2(2.0)} = \frac{81}{4} = 20.25\text{ m}$$
Friction brings the block to rest after an additional $20.25\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Problem 7: Two-force configuration with perpendicular components on a rough plane

hints: Resolve vertically: $R + 40\sin 30^\circ = 15 \times 10 = 150\text{ N}$, so $R = 150 - 20 = 130\text{ N}$.
Calculate limiting friction: $F_r = 0.25 \times 130 = 32.5\text{ N}$.
Total forward horizontal force is $40\cos 30^\circ + 25$.
Net forward force is $40\cos 30^\circ + 25 - 32.5$. Divide by $15\text{ kg}$ to get acceleration.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$R + F_1\sin 30^\circ = mg$$
$$R + 40\sin 30^\circ = 15(10) = 150$$
$$R = 150 - 40(0.5) = 150 - 20 = 130\text{ N}$$

Calculate the frictional resistance opposing motion:
$$F_r = \mu R = 0.25 \times 130 = 32.5\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law in the horizontal direction:
$$F_1\cos 30^\circ + F_2 - F_r = ma$$
$$40\cos 30^\circ + 25 - 32.5 = 15a$$
$$34.641 + 25 - 32.5 = 15a$$
$$27.141 = 15a \implies a = \frac{27.141}{15} \approx 1.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Vertical equilibrium:
$$R = 150 - 40\sin 30^\circ = 130\text{ N}$$

Friction and horizontal components:
$$F_r = 0.25(130) = 32.5\text{ N}$$
$$F_{\text{drive}} = 40\cos 30^\circ + 25 = 34.64 + 25 = 59.64\text{ N}$$

Solve for acceleration:
$$a = \frac{59.64 - 32.5}{15} = \frac{27.14}{15} \approx 1.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The two forward forces combine to accelerate the parcel.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves forces vertically in equilibrium: $R + F_1\sin 30^\circ = mg \implies R + 40(0.5) = 15(10)$.
Shows normal reaction is $R = 150 - 20 = 130\text{ N}$.
Calculates friction force: $F_r = \mu R = 0.25(130) = 32.5\text{ N}$, and resolves horizontally: $F_{\text{forward}} = F_1\cos 30^\circ + F_2 = 40\cos 30^\circ + 25$.
Applies Newton's second law: $40\cos 30^\circ + 25 - 32.5 = 15a \implies 34.641 + 25 - 32.5 = 15a \implies 27.141 = 15a \implies a = 1.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

walkthrough.text:

$$W_{\text{driving}} = (F_1\cos 30^\circ + F_2) s$$
$$W_{\text{driving}} = (40\cos 30^\circ + 25) \times 5.0$$
$$W_{\text{driving}} = (34.641 + 25) \times 5.0 = 59.641 \times 5.0 = 298.2\text{ J} \approx 298\text{ J}$$

Velocity increases under positive net work.

$$W = (34.64 + 25)(5.0) = 59.64(5.0) = 298.2\text{ J} \approx 298\text{ J}$$
The two driving forces together supply $298\text{ J}$ of mechanical energy.
